subject: gk
question: What is one of the major benefits of providing Geographical Indication (GI) tags to local products made by rural artisans?

options.text: It increases dependency on imported goods
It helps preserve traditional knowledge and boosts rural incomes
It removes the need for skill development in rural areas
It allows unrestricted copying of the product by other regions

solution:
The correct answer is __**It helps preserve traditional knowledge and boosts rural incomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Geographical Indication (GI) tags** protect the unique identity of products that are deeply rooted in specific regions, ensuring the preservation of traditional knowledge and skills.
 
• GI tags contribute to **increasing the economic value of artisanal products**, which directly boosts rural incomes and promotes economic stability in rural areas.
 
• They prevent unauthorized use of the registered product name, ensuring that **only authorized producers from the designated region** can market the product under the GI tag.
 
• By granting legal protection to traditional products, GI tags **promote sustainable development** and preserve cultural heritage.
 
• Examples of GI-tagged products in India include **Darjeeling Tea, Channapatna Toys, Kanjeevaram Silk, and Madhubani Paintings**, which are globally recognized for their uniqueness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Indication (GI) Definition:**

 
 
• A GI is a sign used on products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or a reputation due to that origin.
 
• It is governed by the **Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999** in India.
 
 
 
• **Legal Protection:**
 
 
• GI registration provides legal protection to the product, preventing misuse by unauthorized producers.
 
• It ensures **global recognition of locally produced goods** and facilitates access to international markets.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Products with GI tags often command a premium price, benefiting rural artisans and farmers economically.
 
• They help in creating **rural employment opportunities** and ensuring fair trade practices.
 
 
 
• **Notable Examples of GI in India:**
 
 
• Handicrafts: Mysore Silk, Pashmina Shawls, Banarasi Sarees.
 
• Agricultural Products: Alphonso Mango, Basmati Rice, Nagpur Orange.
 
• Food Items: Tirupati Laddu, Hyderabadi Haleem.
 
 
 
• **International Recognition:**
 
 
• GI tags are recognized globally under the **WTO's Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS).**
 
• This ensures that products with GI tags are protected in member countries of the WTO.
